summary: Shadows Left Behind is a browser game that retells the story of NASA's Opportunity rover through Wayang Kulit, Malaysia's traditional shadow puppetry. Using only a webcam, the player's hand becomes the puppet rod: hand tracking moves the shadow puppets in real time, with no controller or install. Players open "Book I: Oppy", wake the rover, scan rocks to reveal real NASA images of Opportunity's discoveries, and carry its memories home to Earth. It turns abandoned hardware on Mars into a story that children and families can feel, and connects space history with Malaysian cultural heritage.
details:
What it does: An interactive shadow-theatre story about NASA's Opportunity rover ("Oppy"), which explored Mars from 2004 to 2018 and now sits silent at Perseverance Valley. The player chooses a storybook (Book I: Oppy is unlocked; Voyager and the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle are planned next), then plays short scenes: wave to sweep dust away and wake Oppy; guide Oppy to a glowing spot with your hand; pinch over rocks to scan them and reveal real NASA images and facts (such as evidence that water once flowed on Mars); and carry Oppy's memories home to Earth, so it is abandoned, but not forgotten. How it works / tools: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with Canvas graphics, hosted on GitHub Pages. Google MediaPipe hand tracking runs in the browser from the webcam; all processing stays on the device and nothing is uploaded. Mouse/touch mode works without a camera. English and Chinese text are supported. Narration uses neural text-to-speech. Why it matters and creativity: Abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars is usually shown as data or photos. Wayang Kulit has told stories with light and shadow for centuries; giving that role to a rover makes its journey personal and memorable, especially for children, while introducing Malaysian heritage to a global audience. Your own hand literally becomes the puppeteer's rod. Benefits and impact: Free, runs in any modern browser, no install, touch-free play, privacy-friendly, and designed to grow into a library of storybooks about discarded space hardware. Factors we considered: young players (big, simple gestures and short scenes), privacy (on-device tracking), accessibility (mouse fallback, captions), and accurate NASA facts and image credits.

Use of SI / AI (disclosure): All narration in the demo video and game is AI-generated text-to-speech (Microsoft neural TTS via edge-tts); the demo video shows a visible "AI-assisted · voices: neural TTS" label. An AI coding assistant (Claude by Anthropic) helped write and debug the code, draw the code-based shadow-puppet art, and edit the English text. Google MediaPipe (machine learning) does on-device hand tracking. All space images are real NASA images, not AI-generated, and no NASA branding was generated or modified.
